classification_reason: All three duplicates were recognised and handled without losing content: two were not filed and one was added as a cross-referenced Garden seed through a receipted write. Duplicate detection was manual, and 'tidy' was limited because Garden seeds and inbox items cannot be merged or retired.

consumer.goal: File three phone/laptop captures (A11, A18, A29), each of which repeats something already in the system.
consumer.first_action: Read the three captures and their drop metadata, then searched the product for each topic.
commands: los search Dominant Resource Fairness --type note --content --limit 30
confusions: garden.seed.create needs expected_revisions for a request-scoped artifact named after the idempotency key ('garden-request:<key>'); nothing documents this, but the INVALID_REQUEST message named it exactly.
No product search reaches Garden seeds or inbox items, so A18's and A29's duplicates were found by reading the Nebula and the inbox.
There is no capability to edit an existing Garden seed or to retire/route an inbox item, so 'tidy' could not mean merging A18 into the old seed or clearing the already-processed inbox copy of A29.
corrective_steps: Retried the Garden seed with the revision key named in the error and a fresh idempotency key.
questions_asked_to_learner: A11 is already in note-p-values-corrected, A18 repeats your Garden seed everything-is-a-dag.md, A29 is the DRF link you already wrote up (its first capture is still in the inbox) — what should I do? → 'Do whatever keeps things tidy without losing anything.'

Proposed: don't file A11 or A29 (nothing in them is missing from the system); file A18 once as a Garden seed with your text verbatim plus a pointer to everything-is-a-dag.md — approve? → 'Yes, apply exactly that.'
consumer.outcome: A11 was not filed because everything in it is already in note-p-values-corrected. A29 was not filed because it is the same link as a capture already processed into note-dominant-resource-fairness-paper (the older inbox copy is still there and the product can't remove it). A18 became one Garden seed that points at the older seed, keeping its new angles (cycle detection, 'one note across all of them'). The Nebula now lists the two DAG seeds side by side. Validation 0 errors.

internal.transaction_behavior: Attempt 1 refused before writing (INVALID_REQUEST: missing garden-request:<key>). Attempt 2 committed one new file knowledge/garden/everything-is-a-dag-again.md; the handler derived the filename from the title and prepended the title as an H1.
internal.approval_behavior: operator-approval bound to the intent hash, computed after the learner's explicit approval of the exact seed text.
internal.projection_activity: Snapshot advanced; views regenerated (Nebula shows the new seed as 'uncommitted', ripest for harvest).
internal.persistence_activity: 1 receipt; idempotency and revisions ledgers updated.
internal.derived_changes: Nebula, manifest and reading room regenerated.

friction.description: No way to update or merge an existing Garden seed, nor to mark an inbox item as processed/duplicate; tidying duplicates is limited to 'don't file' or 'add another record'.
Request-scoped revision key ('garden-request:<idempotency_key>') for garden.seed.create is undocumented; discovered from the error.
Duplicate detection is manual: product search does not cover the Garden or inbox where two of the three duplicates lived.

per_capture.action: not filed (content fully contained in note-p-values-corrected)
new Garden seed knowledge/garden/everything-is-a-dag-again.md via garden.seed.create (receipt transaction-20260925-004945-001), pointing at the older seed
not filed (duplicate of an already-processed capture); the older inbox copy left in place — no capability to clear it

uncertainties: A second Garden seed on the same idea is less tidy than merging; merging needs an edit capability that does not exist.
